plan.summary: No placement is strong enough to carry core budget: the only true pet-subscription publisher (Tailcrate) is a direct competitor, so spend goes to two pet-retail tests — Ruffco for scale and Pawline for subscription-ready pet owners — with everything else excluded for having no link to a new kitten.

test.name: Ruffco
test.rationale: A full-line pet retailer with "repeat-purchase behavior" is the one checkout where a fresh kitten-supply run is actually happening, and $40 sits at roughly half the $73 basket, so the box is an easy add-on; the open question is what share of these 62M impressions are brand-new kitten owners rather than established dog households.

evidence.quote: Largest pet audience in the catalog. Broad demographics, repeat-purchase behavior

test.risk: Shoppers who just stocked up on food and supplies here may feel they already have the toys and samples the box provides, and most of this traffic is existing pet owners, not first-time kitten owners.

test.name: Pawline
test.rationale: Notes say it is "Subscription-heavy" with owners "responsive to premium positioning" — an audience already comfortable with recurring pet billing, and $40 is well under the $64 basket; worth testing whether any meaningful slice are new-kitten households given the 30-55 age skew.

evidence.quote: Subscription-heavy. Owners are health-conscious about pets, responsive to premium positioning

test.risk: Established, health-focused owners on an existing pet subscription are past the new-kitten moment and may see a second pet subscription as redundant; only 4.8M impressions limits learning speed.

test_plan.cut_if: CPA above the $31.20 maximum, or no conversions after 14 days: stop it.

launch_summary.summary: The full $10,000 runs as a test, split evenly between Ruffco ($5,000) for reach across a full-line pet retailer and Pawline ($5,000) for pet owners already comfortable with recurring billing; the only true pet-subscription publisher is a direct competitor, so neither placement was strong enough to be core. The tests are trying to learn what share of each checkout is genuinely new-kitten households rather than established pet owners. All four ads — Pet Parent, Busy Parent, Convenience-First Millennial and Value-Conscious Shopper — run on both, with a 14-day read to promote or cut.
uncertainties: The $40 first order value is assumed, and the $24.00 target and $31.20 maximum cost per new customer are built on it.
Both publishers reach mostly existing pet owners, so the new-kitten moment the offer depends on may be rare in this traffic.
Pawline's 4.8M impressions may not produce enough conversions to judge it within 14 days.
questions: What does the first box actually cost the customer?
Is the box sold only as a subscription, or also as a one-off or gift?
Do you have real margin or lifetime value figures to replace the assumed 60% allowable share?
